    !localStorage.getItem('webfoundry:dev') && (function(c,l,a,r,i,t,y){
      c[a]=c[a]||function(){(c[a].q=c[a].q||[]).push(arguments)};

  <body class="flex flex-col [&>div:first-child]:flex-1 h-[100dvh] pb-[env(safe-area-inset-bottom)]">
    <script type="module">
      (async () => {
        window.rootPrefix = /^\/(files|preview)\//.test(location.pathname) ? location.pathname.split('/').slice(0, 4).join('/') : '/';
        if (rootPrefix === '/' || rootPrefix === '/collab.html') rootPrefix = '.';
        let wforigin = new URL(location.href).searchParams.get('isolate') || location.origin;
        if (/^(\w+\.)?(webfoundry.app|webfoundry\d+\.netlify\.app|localhost)$/.test(wforigin)) throw new Error(`Bad isolation origin`);
        if (new URL(location.href).searchParams.get('isolate') != null) {
          await navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js');
          await navigator.serviceWorker.ready;
          if (!navigator.serviceWorker.controller) return location.reload();
          let parts = location.pathname.slice(1).split('/');
          let tabId = parts[1];
          window.wfThisProject = parts[2];
          navigator.serviceWorker.addEventListener('message', async event => {
            let { type, project, path } = event.data || {};
            if (type !== 'fetch' || wfThisProject !== project) return;
            let port = event.ports?.[0];
            if (!port) return;
            let handler = ev => {
              let data = ev.data || {};
              if (data.type !== 'fetch:res' || data.project !== project || data.path !== path) return;
              removeEventListener('message', handler);
              port.postMessage(data);
            };
            addEventListener('message', handler);
            parent.postMessage({ type: 'fetch', project, path }, wforigin);
          });
          let register = () => navigator.serviceWorker.controller.postMessage({ type:'webfoundry-register-tab', tabId });
          navigator.serviceWorker.addEventListener('controllerchange', register);
          register();
          if (!location.pathname.startsWith('/preview/')) {
            let path = parts.slice(3).join('/');
            if (path !== 'index.html') {
              let handler = async ev => {
                let data = ev.data || {};
                if (data.type !== 'fetch:res' || data.project !== wfThisProject || data.path !== path) return;
                removeEventListener('message', handler);
                document.open();
                document.write(await data.data.text());
                document.close();
              };
              addEventListener('message', handler);
              parent.postMessage({ type: 'fetch', project: wfThisProject, path }, wforigin);
              return;
            }
          }
          await new Promise(pres => setTimeout(pres, 100));
        }
        if (location.pathname.includes('/files/')) return;
        let [, md, mapp] = await Promise.all([
          import(`${rootPrefix}/webfoundry/head.js`),
          import(`${rootPrefix}/webfoundry/dominant.js`),
          import(`${rootPrefix}/webfoundry/app.js`),
        ]);
        document.body.prepend(md.default.el(mapp.default));
        parent.postMessage({ path: `pages/${location.pathname.slice(1).split('/').slice(3).join('/')}`, type: 'ready', status: 200 }, wforigin);
      })();
    </script>
  </body>
</html>

Vessel Software

One developer, two custom frameworks, production-grade results.

I built Dominant and Webfoundry after React handcoding slowed my clients down. Now I ship full sites and apps about 10x faster, with cleaner code and lower delivery cost than a traditional agency.

Watch the Dominant demo Preview Webfoundry builds

How I deliver

Work directly with the engineer who built the tooling. I own discovery, implementation, and iteration without the overhead of agency layers or handoffs.

Custom stack advantage

Dominant and Webfoundry exist because React handcoding was a bottleneck. You get architecture that fits your product instead of conforming to a generic framework.

10x delivery speed

Visual building plus code-level control takes ideas to production in a fraction of the time it takes to handcraft React screens.

Embedded partnership

I plug into your roadmap, keep feedback loops tight, and use live editing sessions so stakeholders always see real progress.

Lean budget impact

A solo delivery model with proprietary tooling means agency polish at a fraction of the cost, no surprise staffing fees.

Dominant

Dominant: my lean engine for complex interfaces

I wrote Dominant because React's abstractions slowed client work to a crawl. Mutable state, direct DOM bindings, and a single update call keep performance tight and the codebase easy to reason about.

  • - Mutate plain objects and call `d.update()` when you want the DOM to react.
  • - Blend with any DOM API, vanilla JS widget, or legacy surface.
  • - Battle-tested on dashboards, marketing sites, and heavy animation demos.
Webfoundry

Webfoundry: 10x faster sites and apps

Webfoundry is my visual builder layered on Dominant. I iterate with clients in the canvas, wire state through controllers, and push production-ready deploys in days, not months.

  • - Visual Tailwind canvas backed by real JavaScript controllers.
  • - `wf-` bindings keep copy, data, and actions in sync as we iterate.
  • - Netlify-ready builds with code quality that holds up long after launch.

I help founders and product teams ship polished software at a fraction of traditional agency cost. Bring an idea or a backlog and I will move it into production quickly.

Discovery Design Build Coach

Reach me directly at hello@vessel.software and let's scope your build.

pages/onepager.html:
Webfoundry — The Creative Operating System for the Modern Web

🚀 Vision

Webfoundry exists to make building for the web feel like play again. We're creating a 10× productivity platform for developers, designers, and creators who want to move fast, iterate visually, and collaborate live — without sacrificing code, control, or performance.

Where Figma stops at design and VS Code stops at code, Webfoundry fuses design, logic, AI assistance, shell access, and deployment into a single real-time creative canvas. This is the missing bridge between imagination and execution.

⚙️ What It Does

Webfoundry is a browser-native, local-first, multiplayer IDE with an intelligent visual editor powered by Tailwind, Trystero WebRTC, and an optional NodeJS Companion server for filesystem and shell integration.

Creators can:

  • Design responsive UIs visually using intuitive Tailwind classes.
  • Edit real project code and visual editor collaboratively, with full HTML/JS/CSS fidelity.
  • Invoke GPT-5.1 Codex via natural voice to patch HTML elements surgically.
  • Run and deploy instantly to Netlify or export to ZIP, desktop (Tauri), or Android (APK).

It’s like if VS Code, Figma, and Replit had a child — one that speaks Tailwind, syncs over P2P, understands your codebase, and treats UI editing and coding as the same continuum.

💡 The Wedge: Ecstaz

Our wedge is Ecstaz — a simple, beautiful, no-setup static site builder that runs entirely inside Webfoundry. Ecstaz is the “Squarespace for the local-first era,” but with a superpower: you can pause the site → drop into Webfoundry visual edit mode → customize everything → resume instantly.

Ecstaz gives Webfoundry the perfect funnel: normie-friendly onboarding with an instant upgrade path into full creative power.

  • Instant page editing with Tiptap and live theme switching.
  • Local storage persistence or full file-system backed editing inside Webfoundry.
  • Export to static HTML, hybrid SPA, or deploy directly from Webfoundry.
  • P2P multiplayer editing out of the box.

Ecstaz and Webfoundry together unlock a new creative workflow: Start simple. Go deep when you're ready. Never switch tools.

🧩 Architecture Advantage

  • Controllers: Modular singletons exposing state and actions globally.
  • P2P Collaboration: Trystero WebRTC mesh syncs edits, selections, and state between peers.
  • Offline-first: LocalForage FS + fetch interception = no backend required.
  • Service Worker Routing: Per-tab app isolation and fast reloads.
  • AI Native: Integrated GPT-5.1 Codex via voice for context-aware code and UI patching.
  • Composable Platform: Ecstaz, slide-deck builders, resume builders, and visual novel engines can all run on top of Webfoundry.

This isn’t a toy or a static site builder — it’s a creative operating system for everything from landing pages to full-stack applications.

📈 Market & Momentum

The $15B web development tools market is fragmenting: design tools, code editors, deployment tools, and AI coding assistants all live in separate worlds. Webfoundry collapses this fragmentation into a single creative workflow.

Early testers are building complex apps in hours instead of days — with multiplayer editing, AI-assisted patching, and zero setup friction.

Ecstaz gives Webfoundry a viral, consumer-friendly entry point that dramatically expands reach.

⏳ Why Now?

  • AI generates code, but no tool lets users edit it visually without breaking it.
  • Local-first computing is exploding: Tauri, PWA, CRDTs, WebRTC.
  • Developers are rejecting heavy frameworks and craving simplicity (Tailwind, HTMX, islands).
  • The gap between “no-code tools” and “real code” is widening. Webfoundry bridges it.
  • Static sites + AI + local-first collaboration is the ecosystem nobody has unified—until now.

Webfoundry is positioned perfectly at the intersection of AI-native editing, local-first tooling, and browser-native creativity.

💬 The Ask

We're assembling early partners and seed investors to accelerate:

  • Team expansion (2 engineers, 1 marketing/growth lead).
  • Public alpha launch of Ecstaz + Webfoundry 5.8.
  • Preparation for YC / Antler and early user acquisition.

We're not just building a tool — we're building the creative engine of the AI-native web.

🌐 webfoundry.app

Contact: gui@guiprav.com
Founder: Gui Prá — Product designer & creative technologist.

08 / Good questions

Just the
important stuff.

Who is Webfoundry for? Do I need to code?+

Webfoundry is a visual IDE for web developers—not a no-code replacement for learning web basics. Tailwind knowledge is enough to build static websites and landing pages. JavaScript lets you build stateful apps, work with controllers, and export supported projects natively.

Can I style visually without memorizing every Tailwind class? +

Yes. Use the styling toolbar for common choices such as typography and colors, or type Tailwind classes directly when that's faster. Webfoundry adds useful visual controls without pretending to be a full no-code CSS designer.

Can I use my own AI coding agent?+

Yes. Bring your coding agent. It can work with ordinary JavaScript files and use Webfoundry's HTML tools for structural edits. Those operations are validated, transactional, undoable, and remain editable on the canvas.

What about collaboration?+

Real-time peer-to-peer collaboration brings people and agents together on the same project. Participants can work independently, with structured changes synced across the session.

Can my app run outside the browser?+

Yes. Supported JavaScript applications can be packaged with Nasty, a native renderer rather than a browser wrapper. Webfoundry also builds ordinary web projects you can publish and host yourself.

Do I need an account to try the editor?+

No. The live demos on this page launch right into the editor. Explore the source, change an element, or play with a controller before signing up for anything.

  1. Select the page root or the element below the header and choose Create Next Sibling. Add classes: bg-slate-950.
  2. Create First Child and add: max-w-6xl mx-auto px-6 py-16 text-white.
  3. Add a heading (set tag to h1) and change text via Single line. Add classes: text-4xl md:text-5xl font-light.
  4. Add a paragraph (set tag to p) and a button (set tag to a with href), style with px-5 py-2 rounded bg-emerald-600 hover:bg-emerald-500.
Editing Content & Media
  • Text: use Text & Media → Single/Multiline.
  • Images: select an img and use Media Gallery to swap visuals quickly.
  • Backgrounds: for sections, use Background Gallery to apply imagery.
Styling with Tailwind
Compose utilities in the Styles panel and Tailwind toolbar:
  • Typography: text-xl md:text-2xl font-semibold tracking-wide
  • Layout: flex items-center justify-between gap-4
  • Spacing: px-6 py-4 md:px-10
  • Colors: bg-slate-900 text-white/90 hover:bg-white/10
Restructure & Reuse
  • Wrap: add a parent wrapper around the selection to group content.
  • Create: insert first/last child or next/prev siblings to build structure.
  • Paste: duplicate elements and move them around your layout.
Preview & Iterate
  • Toggle Preview to view the page as users will see it (if not visible, see the visibility notes above).
  • Return to edit mode to adjust text, classes, and structure.
Files & Saving
  • Use Files to create, rename, and organize items under pages/.
  • Open any HTML under pages/ to start editing it visually.
Advanced (Optional)
  • Conditional and Map (Toolbar → JavaScript) can show/hide or repeat blocks once you’re ready to add dynamic views.
  • Event handlers can be attached from dialogs when you need simple interactivity.

Quickstart: Create, Style, Publish

In ~10 minutes you’ll create your first project, add a page, style a section’s background, and see where to deploy it.

Prereqs: use a desktop‑width viewport to see the top toolbar (Tailwind & Manipulation).
  1. Create a project
    Open Projects (left rail) → Create. Give it a friendly name in Settings & More → Project Title.
  2. See pages/index.html load
  3. Delete the placeholder and create your first div
    Select the placeholder element that says "Page intentionally left blank."
    Click placeholder element then: Top toolbar → Manipulation → Delete (cross icon).
  4. Insert a section to style
    Top toolbar → Manipulation → Create → Inside. Select <section> from the tag dropdown.
  5. Give it a background color
    Switch to the Tailwind toolbar → Back Color (pick a hue) → Back Shade (e.g., 500). You’ll see background change immediately.
    Alternate: open the Styles panel (left raild) → “add class” → type bg-blue-500.
  6. Preview & publish (later)
    For now, note that the Deploy flow lives under Settings & More → Deploy to Netlify. We’ll cover it in detail below.
What you learned
  • Projects vs Files vs Designer.
  • Two ways to style: Tailwind menus or Styles panel.
  • Where the Deploy flow lives.

Building Pages

Select, navigate, and restructure quickly; then edit text and media.

1) Navigate selection
  • Manipulation → Cursor: Parent, Next, Previous, First/Last Child.
  • Optional Vim/arrow keys: h (left arrow key) parent, j (down arrow key) next, k (up arrow key) previous, l (right arrow key)/L child/last child.
2) Restructure fast
  • Manipulation → Create: Inside, Inside (last), After, Before.
  • Wrap gathers selection into a new parent; Unwrap removes a wrapper.
  • Use Delete/Copy buttons in the toolbar for quick cleanup and duplication.
3) Edit content
  • Text & Media → Single line / Multiline to replace text nodes.
  • Links: Link URL on anchors (<a>).
  • Images & backgrounds: Media URL, Media Gallery, and Background URL/Gallery.
4) Style with Tailwind
  • Font Family (includes Google Fonts search), Text Size/Style/Tracking.
  • Text Color + Shade; Back Color + Shade.
  • Or add classes directly via the Styles panel (supports inline editing/renaming).

Files & Editing

Create/rename/delete: use the Files panel controls. Protected items are hidden from rename/delete.

Drag & drop: rearrange files/folders; the UI shows valid drop targets as you drag.

Media preview: selecting images/videos/audio opens a live preview pane.

Code editor: non‑HTML text files open in a code area. Use it for scripts, JSON, etc.

Interactivity

You can add logic via declarative attributes—no manual DOM plumbing.

A. Conditional rendering (wf‑if)
  1. Select an element you want to show/hide.
  2. Toolbar → JavaScript → Conditional and set an expression (e.g., state.app.ready).
Effect: the element toggles in/out when the expression truthiness changes.
B. Lists (wf‑map)
  1. Insert a container where items should render.
  2. Toolbar → JavaScript → Map and set item of state.todos.
  3. Inside it, use mustache to show fields: {{item.text}}.
C. Events (wf‑on*)
  1. Select a button or input.
  2. Toolbar → JavaScript → Event Handlers, e.g., set click to post('app.save').
Tip: Handler values are expressions (not statements). For complex flows, call actions (post('ctrl.action')).
D. Forms
  • Placeholder (Element → Placeholder) for inputs/textarea.
  • Set Input Value to bind values (two‑way with wf‑value).
  • Form Method (GET/POST) when a form is selected.

Global & Project Settings

Wallpaper & brand: define a background URL for the editor; toggle brand canvas visibility when nothing is open.

Titles: set Project Title and Page Title for clarity in the header/HTML <title>.

Toolbar: hidden on small screens; show/hide on desktop via Settings.

Vim: enable Vim keybindings for selection navigation.

Per‑project options: NerdFonts, Tailwind, Better Chrome Scrollbars, Peacock (accent).

Netlify Deploys

Publish in minutes. Use Preview for drafts and Production for your real site.

  1. Open Deploy to Netlify (Settings & More). If prompted, set the Netlify API key.
  2. Select an existing site or choose Create new site and enter a name.
  3. Pick Production or Deploy Preview and click Deploy.
  4. Use the post‑deploy dialog to open Preview/Production links (and copy them for sharing).
Tip: Keep Preview deploys for feature branches. Switch to Production once you’re happy.

Git & ZIP Import/Export

Import Git (HTTPS)
  1. Settings & More → Import Git (HTTPS).
  2. Paste the repo URL. Wait for branches; pick one.
  3. Provide a project name if requested, then Import.
Import / Export ZIP
  • Import ZIP to load an archive into your project space.
  • Export ZIP to share or back up your project quickly.

Realtime Collaboration

Invite others to co‑edit with presence and a collab‑aware toolbar.

  1. If available, open Collaborate in Settings & More to get a share link.
  2. Send the link to your peer. They’ll open a collab UI that shows presence and selection state.
  3. Footer indicates “Awaiting collaborators…” or “Collaborating with N peers.”
Note: Some setups require Cross‑origin isolation for RTC; toggle it in Settings when available.

Companion, Shell, Companion FS

Enable Companion in Settings to unlock the Shell (integrated terminal).

The Shell panel supports multiple tabs. If authentication fails, you’ll see a warning row with a Retry button and guidance to reconfigure the key.

Companion FS can store the project via the Companion’s filesystem—toggle it per project in Settings.

Database Collections

Organize collections of data for your app.

  • Create, rename, or delete collections from the DB panel.
  • Select a collection to view/edit (when your setup supports editing the data shape).

Tips & Shortcuts

Keyboard
  • Undo / Redo: Ctrl‑Z / Ctrl‑Y.
  • Vim movement (optional): h j k l L.
Troubleshooting
  • Toolbar missing? Switch to a desktop width or show the toolbar in Settings.
  • Busy spinner? Wait for operations to complete; avoid rapid, conflicting actions.
  • Companion auth fail? Use Retry or reconfigure the key in Settings.
Examples
Expressions you might set in dialogs: 

wf-if:          state.app.ready
wf-map:         item of state.items
wf-onclick:     post('app.addItem')
wf-disabled:    !form.valid
